headline: Every carton of boxed beef checked, not a sample.
formProduct: Chilled and frozen boxed beef, export cartons
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to one of your plants
heroLede: With cartons leaving your plants in Victoria and Tasmania for export and local customers every day, the cut, label and date on every carton has to match the order. Here's what a camera check could look like on your carton lines. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every carton is closed and taped flat before it reaches the chiller, with no flap lifted and no bag showing. A carton that opens in transit is a claim from the customer.
labelLede: A striploin carton and a cube roll carton look the same from the outside. The camera checks every carton carries the right label for the cut being packed, straight and readable.
codeLede: Export and local cartons carry a packed-on date and lot code that have to be right on every carton. The system reads the printed date and lot on every carton and compares them with what was set for the run.
objectLede: Knife sheaths, glove pieces, tape and liner offcuts are all close at hand in a carton room. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before cartons are palletised.

vocab.alert: Four lifted flaps in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the carton taper.
